#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Simplifies the setup in the integration test for node lifecycle manager. In particular:
- uses "NodeDisruptionExclusion" feature instead of  periodic heartbeat events to simplify the logic, it was also requested in this comment:
```
			// Regularly send heartbeat event to APIServer so that the cluster doesn't enter fullyDisruption mode.
			// TODO(Huang-Wei): use "NodeDisruptionExclusion" feature to simply the below logic when it's beta.
```
- eliminates scheduler from this test
- replaces the custom code for awaiting for a condition with built-in wait.PollImmediate()

issue_context.title: Simplify the "TestTaintBasedEvictions" integration test in lifecycle_test.go
issue_context.body:
The following things should be simplified:
- use "NodeDisruptionExclusion" feature instead of  periodic heartbeat events to simplify the logic, it was also requested in this comment:
```
			// Regularly send heartbeat event to APIServer so that the cluster doesn't enter fullyDisruption mode.
			// TODO(Huang-Wei): use "NodeDisruptionExclusion" feature to simply the below logic when it's beta.
```
- eliminate scheduler from this test

/remove-sig apps
/sig node

It looks like this test is actually using the scheduler. But I don't think it should. The pods should be created with NodeName.

review_comments: Agree, removed the outer `i`, don't need to index the pod across test cases
yeah, this is weird, why wasn't part of the struct before?

It seems for 'historical reasons'. I've traced it back to this commit https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/ca10e616bf88ee0f0ed00762c92948761dd56d62. It seems the test was first added as a non-table e2e test. Later it was converted to a table integration test, but the list was not refactored. Seems reasonable to do it now.
agreed, it is much better this way
it's better if we do not conflate unrelated changes on the same commit
I think replacing the Errorf with Fatalf for setup makes the test simpler (which is the goal of the PR).

yeah, but think that those are 2 different tests, if we somehow figure out after merge that we broke something, we have to revert the commit, and we want to revert only the code that break something,
In this case, you should have one commit per test, we somehow organize commits per topic to facilitate reviews, but keeping a clean git history helps the code maintenance , is not a big deal in this case, but hygiene always help

I get the point about keeping commits isolated and clean. However, I think in this case
case it makes sense to apply the same changes to both tests in the file (`TestTaintBasedEvictions` and `TestEvictionForNoExecuteTaintAddedByUser`):
- move `nodeIndex` next to `nodeCount`
- add a comment to `nodeIndex`
- using Fatalf instead of Errorf 

Applying them to only one of the tests would make another reader puzzled it seems.
I've split the changes into two separate commits within the PR. Hope it makes sense.
ah ok, then I misread it, sorry for the obvious comment then :smile:
are you sure this line is not necessary?

Yes, actually we cannot even call it in the current setup. because the function calls `Start` and `WaitForCacheSync` on `testCtx.InformerFactory` which is nil in this test (after getting rid of scheduler). 
However, using this function could replace the two lines above `externalInformers.Start(testCtx.Ctx.Done())` and `externalInformers.WaitForCacheSync(testCtx.Ctx.Done())`  if we earlier assigned `testCtx.InformerFactory = externalInformers`, but it isn't a clear gain to me. The function `SyncInformerFactory` seems to only be used by tests for Scheduler currently.
